span.p:
Prediction 'what will Y be?' — P(Y | X)
vs
Causal 'what if we set X = x?' — P(Y | do(X))
different quantities, in general

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

p.small: a common cause Z of both X and Y creates an association even when X has no effect on Y (Simpson's paradox, §2)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p:
Potential Outcomes (Rubin) · §3
τ = Y(1) − Y(0) per unit · the fundamental problem: you only ever observe one of Y(1), Y(0)

div.style: color: rgb(237, 230, 215) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p:
Structural Causal Models / DAGs (Pearl) · §4
P(Y | do(X)) = delete X's incoming edges, then read off Y

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p: Conditional independence in a graph — chains, forks, colliders · §5

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p: d-separation — a complete, mechanical procedure for every conditional independence · §6

div.style: color: rgb(237, 230, 215) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p: do-calculus — three rules that reduce a do(·) expression to an observational one, when the graph permits · §7

span.p: Backdoor / frontdoor adjustment — the two ready-made recipes built from those rules · §8

span.p: RCTs — randomise and sidestep identification entirely, at a cost in money, ethics and generalizability · §9
